---
title: "Syntax"
---

A working reference for Jestyr's surface syntax. Every construct on this
page compiles under the current toolchain; most are lifted from the
[example programs](tour.qmd), which remain the authoritative demos.
Files use the `.jtr` extension. Comments are `// line comments`
(doc comments are `///`, picked up by `jestyrc doc`). Statements end at
newlines — no semicolons.

## Bindings and primitive types

```{.rust}
let x: i32 = 42        // immutable binding
var y: i64 = -5        // mutable binding
y = y + 1

let big: i64 = 9000000000
let n: usize = 10      // sizes and indices
let byte: u8 = 255
let f: f64 = 2.5
let ok: bool = true
let s: str = "a view"  // borrowed string view
```

Integer types: `i32`, `i64`, `u8`, `u64`, `usize` (and friends).
Floating point is `f64` under a [locked determinism contract](determinism.qmd).
Conversions are explicit, spelled `as`:

```{.rust}
let i: i32 = 7
let u: usize = i as usize
let d: f64 = i as f64
```

## Functions and parameter conventions

The default parameter convention is `read` — an immutable borrow. Only
`take` transfers ownership; `mut` borrows exclusively. This is the whole
ownership surface most code sees (see [Safety](safety.qmd)):

```{.rust}
fn area(read r: Rect) -> i64 { return r.w * r.h }   // borrow (default)
fn grow(mut r: Rect)        { r.w = r.w * 2 }       // exclusive borrow
fn consume(take r: Rect)    { /* owns r; drops it */ }
```

Contracts ride on the signature and lower to checked asserts:

```{.rust}
fn clamp(x: i32, lo: i32, hi: i32) -> i32
    requires lo <= hi
    ensures result >= lo
{
    if x < lo { return lo }
    if x > hi { return hi }
    return x
}
```

## Control flow

`if` / `else if` / `else` are expressions of the usual shape; `for` is
the single unified loop — condition loops, range loops, slice loops, and
infinite loops are all `for`:

```{.rust}
if a < -1 { b = 1 } else if a == 0 { b = 2 } else { b = 3 }

var i: i32 = 0
for i < 10 { i = i + 1 }        // while-style: for <condition>

for k in 0..5 { print_int(k) }  // range (0..=5 includes the end)

for read x in xs { print_int(x) }  // borrow each element
for mut x in xs { x = x + 1 }      // exclusive borrow, mutate in place
for x in s { total = total + x }// iterate a slice

for { break }                    // infinite, with break/continue
```

A search loop can carry an `else` (runs when the loop finds nothing and
exits normally) — see `examples/loops_else.jtr`.

## Structs, enums, match

```{.rust}
struct Point { x: i64, y: i64 }
let p: Point = Point { x: 3, y: 4 }
let q: Point = Point { x: 9, ..p }      // struct update / spread

enum Shape {
    circle(r: i64),
    rect(w: i64, h: i64),
    empty,
}

fn area(read s: Shape) -> i64 {
    match s {                            // exhaustiveness is CHECKED
        circle(r)  => 3 * r * r,
        rect(w, h) => w * h,
        empty      => 0,
    }
}
```

Recursive enums box their children explicitly with `indirect` — Jestyr
never hides an allocation:

```{.rust}
enum Expr {
    lit(v: i32),
    add(l: indirect Expr, r: indirect Expr),
}
```

`match` also supports guards, or-patterns, rest-patterns, and scalar
matches with `_` catch-alls (`examples/{guards,orpat,rest_pat}.jtr`).
`distinct` makes zero-cost newtypes (`distinct UserId = i32`) that do
not interconvert silently; `record` declares immutable-by-construction
values.

## Arrays, slices, strings

```{.rust}
var board: [64]i32 = [0; 64]     // fixed array: a stack VALUE
board[3] = 1                     // bounds-checked indexing

let s: []i64 = slice(i64, ptr, n)  // slice: a fat-pointer view
print_int(s.len as i64)

let view: str = "hello"           // str borrows; String owns
var owned: String = string_from("Hello")
string_push(owned, ", world")
print_str(string_view(owned))     // lend the buffer as a view
string_free(owned)

for w in split("a,bb", ",") { print_int(w.len as i64) }  // zero-copy
```

Bounds checks elide only when a refinement proof covers the index
(`i in 0..s.len` — `examples/refine.jtr`).

## Errors: sets, payloads, `?`, `catch`

Error sets are part of the signature; names can carry one payload value,
stack-only:

```{.rust}
fn parse(n: i64) -> i64 !{ Empty, TooBig(i64) } {
    if n == 0  { return err(Empty) }
    if n > 99  { return err(TooBig(n)) }   // the payload rides along
    return ok(n * 2)
}

fn hop(n: i64) -> i64 !{ Empty, TooBig(i64) } {
    let v = parse(n)?          // propagate: set inclusion is CHECKED
    return ok(v + 1)
}

// recover, extracting payloads exhaustively:
let r: i64 = hop(500) catch |e| match e {
    Empty     => -1,
    TooBig(v) => v,
}

let d: i64 = hop(0) catch -1   // or just a default
```

Error sets appear in trait signatures too — see the
[ledger example](tour.qmd) — and `--error-traces` records the
propagation path.

## Generics, traits, dynamic dispatch

```{.rust}
fn describe[T: Show](read x: T) -> i32 { ... }  // bound, monomorphized
fn dup[T](take x: T) -> T { return x }          // unbounded generic

trait Account {
    fn withdraw(read self, amt: i64) -> i64 !{ Insufficient(i64) }
}

impl Account for Checking {
    fn withdraw(read self, amt: i64) -> i64 !{ Insufficient(i64) } {
        if amt > self.balance { return err(Insufficient(self.balance)) }
        return ok(self.balance - amt)
    }
}

fn spend[T: Account](read acct: T, amt: i64) -> i64 { ... }  // static
fn show(read s: dyn Shape) { ... }                            // vtable
```

Generic structs (`struct List(T)`) monomorphize per instance; methods
live in `impl` blocks and call with dot syntax. Function-pointer types
and closures (`|| use(x)`) are first-class (`examples/{fn_ptr,closures}.jtr`).

## References beyond borrows

```{.rust}
// genref: storable, generation-checked — use-after-free FAULTS
var r: &i32 = gen_new(i32, 42)
print_int(r.*)
gen_free(r)

// region: zero-cost arena refs, escape is a compile error
region a {
    var p: &[a]Point = region_alloc(a, Point, Point { x: 1, y: 2 })
    print_int(p.*.x)
}   // whole arena freed here, O(1)
```

## Concurrency and parallelism

```{.rust}
concurrent {              // structured: joins ALL tasks at the brace
    spawn worker(buf, 0)
    spawn worker(buf, 1)
}

atomic_add(counter, 1)    // atomics for shared accumulation

@span(log) fn sum_sq(read s: []i64) -> i64 {
    par for x in s reduce(core.sum_reduction()) { x * x }
}
```

`par for` accepts only *declared-deterministic* reductions — a
non-deterministic one is a compile error, and serializing a `par for`
back to `for` violates its `@span` contract, also a compile error.
Channels, `select`, task handles with `await`, and dynamic spawn counts
round out the surface (`examples/std/{channel,select,await}.jtr`).

## Compile-time evaluation

```{.rust}
const SIZE: i64 = 8
let a: i64 = comptime { fact(10) }          // evaluated while compiling
const SQ: [6]i64 = comptime { [sq(0), sq(1), sq(2), sq(3), sq(4), sq(5)] }
```

The evaluator is total: step budgets and call-depth caps make a runaway
definition a diagnostic, not a hung build.

## Attributes

| attribute | meaning |
|---|---|
| `@no_alloc` | proven allocation-free, transitively — violations are compile errors |
| `@span(log)` / `@span(linear)` | checked work-span cost class |
| `@simd` | checked vectorization legality |
| `@deterministic` | rejects non-deterministic reductions |
| `@packed`, `@align(n)`, `@layout(auto)` | memory layout control |
| `@volatile`, `@address(0x…)` | bare-metal / MMIO |
| `@test`, `@bench` | the built-in test harness (`jestyrc test`) |

See [the attributes doc](https://github.com/AdamEzzat1/Jestyr/blob/master/docs/attributes.md)
for the full catalogue with the compile-error examples.

## `unsafe` and raw pointers

Raw pointers (`*mut T`, `*const T`) exist for FFI, MMIO, and allocator
internals. Every dereference must sit inside an `unsafe` block — outside
one it is a compile error, on both toolchains:

```{.rust}
var p: *mut i32 = alloc(i32, 4)
unsafe { (p + 2).* = 7 }
let v: i32 = unsafe { (p + 2).* }
free_ptr(p)

extern "c" fn abs(x: i32) -> i32     // C interop by bare name
```

The obligations a raw pointer carries are written down in
[the unsafe contract](https://github.com/AdamEzzat1/Jestyr/blob/master/docs/unsafe-contract.md).

## Modules

```{.rust}
import "../std/mem"                  // path import
import "helpers" as h                // alias
import "vendored" = "3f9c…"          // content-hash-pinned

let a: Allocator = mem.system_allocator()   // qualified access
```

`pub` controls visibility; a directory can be a module; the module graph
is content-hashed and can be pinned like a lockfile. The self-hosted
compiler loads its own ten-module closure through this system.
